decisions.question:
How should the water-food trade-off be resolved in arid and
semi-arid regions?
decisions.title: Arid-region water allocation vs. food self-sufficiency

decisions.question:
When budgets conflict (land, water, energy, labor), what should the
joint resource balance sheet treat as the fixed constraint and what as the flexing
variable?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Population is the output variable; water/land/energy/labor
budgets are the constraints.
decisions.title: Joint resource balance sheet: framing precedent

decisions.question:
How should the 20–30% biomass polymer pillar be sourced, and what
happens to the 15% arable-land cap?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Residue-first sourcing; 15% cap replaced outright with a 5%
exception-only cap; food-branch land-surplus certification no longer required.
decisions.title: Biomass polymer feedstock sourcing vs. food land

decisions.question:
How should the node handle the four-authority arbitration gap before
Domain III exists?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Formal problem specification written; mechanism explicitly
deferred; Domain III owns the mechanism question, the node owns the problem.
decisions.title: Sectoral authority arbitration: problem specified, mechanism deferred

decisions.question:
How should the nuclear share be handled in water-stressed arid
regions to break the dry-cooling efficiency feedback loop?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Nuclear share tiered by water stress; hybrid dry cooling
mandated in stressed regions; displaced share filled by solar+storage overbuild
and HVDC imports.
decisions.title: Nuclear share under dry cooling in water-stressed regions

decisions.question:
How should freight be assigned to modes given the restated
4,000–6,000 kWh/cap/yr buildings+transport electricity band — by price signals
 alone, or by structure?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Rail-vs-road gap (~65–115 kWh/cap/yr on arid grain-band
freight alone; rail 0.03–0.05 vs road 0.7–1.0 kWh/t-km) is the binding lever —
mode structure, not price.
decisions.title: Freight allocation mechanism: modal hierarchy vs. road pricing

decisions.question:
Do the node's three largest freight flows ride one shared
corridor class or three per-sector logistics networks?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Booked-not-traded capacity on shared spines; grain band and
ammonia reservations precede discretionary freight.
decisions.title: One freight spine class (≥1.5 Mt/yr corridors) shared by grain band, ammonia, and components

decisions.question:
Should the Regional Transport Authority be designed as a fourth
sectoral authority now, with the collision table extended, or left unspecified
until Domain III?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A; the authority-arbitration spec gains the RTA rows (to be
inserted at the next revision of that file).
decisions.title: RTA joins the sectoral-authority set; three new collision rows

decisions.question:
(a) Who gets the declining e-fuel budget, and (b) do critical
goods carry buffer stock or ride just-in-time plus emergency response?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A both parts. Sixth resource class (critical-goods buffers)
joins the no-market/allocated lineage (energy, water primary allocation, and
spine capacity precede it).
decisions.title: e-Fuel allocation order and buffer-stock extension of the no-market lineage

decisions.question:
DEC-009 mandated a six-week buffer of "critical goods" but left
"critical" example-defined. How is the buffer class defined so it can't expand
into general social overhead?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Node buffer arithmetic (2M-person region): grain
25–29 kt, ammonia 1.2–1.8 kt, treatment chemicals 0.2–0.4 kt, medicines
0.1–0.4 kt — total 27–32 kt, ~15–40 M USD of node warehouse structure, plus
~6–14 kWh/cap/yr cold-chain electricity inside the buildings+transport band.
decisions.title: Storage classification: closed four-class system vs. qualitative "critical goods"

decisions.question:
Who allocates scarce storage during flow interruptions — booked
reservations or a storage market?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Storage joins the no-financial-markets lineage (energy
PPAs, water hierarchy, spine capacity booking) as its allocated-infrastructure
instance.
decisions.title: Storage capacity booked like track; one stock ledger per region

decisions.question:
Does the grain band — a designed, firm-delivery dependency —
carry a supplier-diversity requirement like the materials log's, and at what
threshold?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. The 60% threshold is a deliberate, named relaxation of the
materials log's 40% supplier floor for substitutable origins.
decisions.title: Dual-origin rule for the grain band and other monoflows

decisions.question:
Are Class B stock levels public, and does interruption response
run on pre-written protocols or operator discretion?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A, status tentative — the publication cadence and rationing
pre-delegation both need confirmation from Domain II (negotiation design) and
Domain IV (legal recognition) before firming. Flagged as the first
cross-domain-confirmation purchase since DEC-001; nothing in I.1/I.2 depends on
it before that confirmation.
decisions.title: Stock publicity and pre-written interruption protocols (tentative)

decisions.question:
When a scarce input must be curtailed, who is protected and in
what order — pre-agreed classes or case-by-case boards?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Real-world basis: the EU's 2022 gas demand-reduction
regulation (Council Regulation (EU) 2022/1854) protected-consumer classes —
worked because pre-agreed, not negotiated mid-crisis.
decisions.title: Priority classes for curtailable scarce inputs

decisions.question:
At what numeric thresholds does goods rationing activate, and
who holds the ladder?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A, ladder stages firm; the R3 famine-commons mechanism
itself is Domain II's to design (existing DEC-001 mutual-famine-security
residue — the food log's own open tension: if Domain II cannot guarantee
famine-secure band delivery, R3's arithmetic changes and the ladder is
revised).
decisions.title: Food/goods ration ladder with pre-numeric triggers

decisions.question:
How does the ordinary (Class C) consumer economy allocate when
a good goes scarce — price escalation or ration-by-points?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Points architecture is an in-kind instrument, not a
currency: transfer prohibited, expiry mandatory — Domain II designs retail
channels and the instrument's accounting class.
decisions.title: Class C ordinary goods: fixed prices, non-transferable points, no price rationing

decisions.question:
Who administers an active ration ladder, and how is it
enforced?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A, tentative — needs Domain III's arbitration-mechanism
fit and Domain IV's civil-process confirmation before firming, per the
storage log's pre-delegation pattern. Second cross-domain-confirmation
purchase of the node (after DEC-013); nothing depends on it before that
confirmation.
decisions.title: Ration administration rides the RTA's machinery; civil-claims enforcement (tentative)

decisions.question:
The I.2 integration review ended "Not settled" with a 7-item
resolution list; with a one-work-package-per-session discipline, which item
does this session take first?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Session shape confirmed in-session as: amend the
transport log (Decision 1 of the session, DEC-019) and, in the same session,
recompute the R-ladder against the corrected corridor arithmetic and amend
storage + allocation logs (DEC-020) — because the buffer sits on spine nodes
whose qualifying threshold just changed; leaving the ladder unfixed between
sessions would leave the repo knowingly holding an emergency plan that runs
dry before its most serious stage.
decisions.title: Integration-fix session scoping: which resolution item first

decisions.question:
Transport Decision 2 admits corridors to spine status at
≥1.5 Mt/yr forecast load, but an arid region's named node flows (grain band
0.22–0.25 Mt/yr, own-food ammonia ~13 kt/yr, steel/components 0.4–0.6 Mt/yr)
sum to ≈0.7–1.1 Mt/yr even double-counted — while the same decision text
claims arid regions get "spine build-out priority" under that test. How do
arid corridors qualify?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Amended into `01-2-1_transport-of-goods-full.md`
(Decision 2 amendment block) and the Transport log §1 (AMENDED entry). The
≥1.5 Mt/yr test stands for regions with navigable water or dense corridor
networks; arid/non-navigable regions qualify at ≥0.5 Mt/yr. All other spine
rules unchanged: designation cycle, booked capacity, tripartite board, buffer
siting at spine nodes, warehouse fit-out. A 10-year spine review may re-tier
a region whose flow mix crosses classes.
decisions.title: Arid tier for the spine eligibility threshold (I.2.1 revision)

decisions.question:
The R-ladder's age-based triggers (R1 >2 wk; R2 >4 wk; R3
>8 wk) scheduled the full-emergency stage R3 two weeks after the
buffer's full-stretch exhaustion (~wk 5.65–6.03, verified by recompute);
R3's stated sustenance premise ("buffer at full stretch") was therefore
arithmetically false exactly at the ladder's failure mode. How is the ladder
re-cut?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-A. Amended into `01-2-3_allocation-mechanisms-full.md`
(Decision 2 ladder rewrite + amendment block) and the Allocation log §1
(AMENDED entry); the Storage log §2 gains a RESOLVED cross-ref (its quarterly
stock publication is now the ladder's primary trigger surface; annual
stock-ledger audit reviews the freeboard threshold value).
decisions.title: Ration-ladder triggers re-anchored to buffer state (I.2.3 + I.2.2 revision)

decisions.question:
The node holds three published scarcity-ordering schemes with
no crosswalk governing co-occurring scarcity — the water log's allocation
hierarchy + staged drought protocol (env. flows > domestic > essential >
ag > industrial > non-essential; Stage 3 cap 150 L/p/d, Stage 4 50 L/p/d),
Allocation Decision 1's P1–P4 priority classes (life-support > critical
infrastructure > food-chain > everything else), and transport Decision 3's
e-fuel order (aviation first, shipping second, surplus to ag machinery) —
and the register carries no e-fuel priority class. Overlapping claimants
sit at different heights on different ladders (agriculture below domestic
on water but P3 on inputs; industrial P4 on goods but above non-essential
on water). Who owns the crosswalk, which ladder governs co-occurring
scarcity, and what class do e-fuels carry?
decisions.recorded_decision:
all three alt-A's (A / 1 / A as presented in the
interview rounds). Recorded as DEC-021.1 (allocation owns, register
hosts), DEC-021.2 (per-resource precedence, no supremacy clause,
compound case → spec §2.11), DEC-021.3 (mission-propelled class).
Amended into `01-2-3_allocation-mechanisms-full.md` (Decision 1
amendment block + §1 AMENDED mirror entry + §2 residual), the Allocation
log (§1 AMENDED entry + §2 residual), the Water log and Transport log
(each a cross-ref entry + mirrored full-doc §3 line), and the arbitration
spec (§2.11 row added).
decisions.title: Scarcity-ladder crosswalk: ownership, governing rule, e-fuel class (I.2.3 fix, resolves Contradiction C)

decisions.question:
The RTA now holds nine functions (track, catenary, licensing,
spine designation, buffer custody, classification register, storage ledger,
WMS, priority classes — plus ration administration added by I.2.3), each
branch's concentration flag having assessed only its own slice; the
integration review §4 finding 1 diagnoses the compounded institution as the
essay's concentrated-institution decay profile at its strongest, and rules
the node needs a deliberate RTA-span review (I.1's Blocker-2-equivalent)
or an intra-RTA division design. How is the nine-function concentration
resolved, given that the arbitration spec §5 binds the node against adding
a sixth sectoral authority until Domain III answers?
decisions.recorded_decision:
alt-1 (internal division) + alt-2.1 (dual-key KPI review) +
alt-A (selective amendment). Recorded as **DEC-022.1** (two divisions,
function map below), **DEC-022.2** (dual-key review machinery), and
**DEC-022.3** (selective-amendment propagation scope).
decisions.title: RTA span review: two internal divisions + dual-key decay review (resolves I.2 integration §4 finding 1, resolution item 6)

decisions.question: A full re-run of the session check across the ledger found four log↔full asymmetries from the 2026-10-11 DEC-019/020 integration-fix session: (1) the Transport log §1 never received the DEC-019 amended spine entry (the Transport full's closing block has it, and the DEC-019 record and CL-012 say the log does); (2) the Transport full's §2 arid-gap bullet still reads "resolution waits on Domain III" — stale against its own §1 entry and the log; (3) the Storage full never received the DEC-020 resolved cross-ref its log carries; (4) the Allocation full's closing block carries the DEC-021 amended mirror entry but not the DEC-020 one. How much does the pass repair?
decisions.recorded_decision: alt-A. Repairs applied same session: (1) DEC-019 amended entry restored to `01-2-1_transport-of-goods-log.md` §1, verbatim from the Transport full's closing block; (2) the Transport full §2 arid-gap bullet updated to the resolved state (arid tier ≥0.5 Mt/yr; residual: exact spine list waits on Domain III; ammonia-denominator tail kept); (3) DEC-020 resolved cross-ref mirrored into `01-2-2_storage-supply-chains-full.md` §2; (4) DEC-020 amended entry mirrored into `01-2-3_allocation-mechanisms-full.md`'s closing block at the log's position, text verbatim.
decisions.title: Reconciliation pass: repair all four log↔full asymmetries (DEC-019/020 era)

The check matches canonical labels, so re-auditing any of the first twenty decisions reports every rejected option as unindexed. What happens to the older labels?

SKILL.md pitfall note updated to record the boundary.
